summary: No criminalisation of trans presence. The state congress passed a 2024 reform amending the Civil Code to create an administrative legal gender recognition procedure, and Campeche's legislature recognises the transfemicide offence. No dedicated incident, enforcement or ordinance evidence was found; visitor-facing risk tracks the national baseline.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition in Mexico (March 2025), covering which of the 32 states have legislated an administrative procedure and the Supreme Court rulings that drove expansion. For Campeche: a 2024 Civil Code reform created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure.

Human Rights Watch report 'I Just Want to Contribute to Society' (6 March 2024) on Tabasco: no legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional mistreatment - the August 2023 killing of activist Karina Gomez remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from Tabasco's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. Baseline for how a non-reforming state behaves.

Guardian report (24 July 2024) on Mexico City making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (the 'Paola Buenrostro law', approved 18 July 2024), in one of Latin America's deadliest settings for trans people; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.

localsOnly: The 2024 legal gender recognition reform and transfemicide-offence recognition are resident-facing civil-registry and criminal-law machinery.
